---README---
# Mine

A set of small PWAs that keep your personal data as markdown in a private GitHub repo —
calendar, zettelkasten, diary — so it stays portable and free of vendor lock-in.

**Live: https://maximilianharr.github.io/mine/** — install it to your home screen.

## Docs

| | |
| --- | --- |
| [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) | what the app does and how it behaves |
| [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) | how it is built, and the verified platform findings |
| [TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md](TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md) | what is checked before a change ships, and how |
| [calendar/](calendar/) | the calendar app, with its own pair of docs |

## Layout

```
style.css                                         the shared base: tokens and chrome
index.html app.js home.css sw.js manifest.json    the main app
shared/   apps.js store.js github.js md.js        used by every app
          markdown.js prefs.js ui.js sync.js
          vendor/
calendar/                                         one folder per app
spike/                                            on-device platform checks
test/                                             the checks: test/run.sh
```

No build step: no bundler, no CI, no dependencies to install. `git push` deploys to GitHub
Pages. To run it locally, `python3 -m http.server` in this folder and open the printed URL.
`test/run.sh` runs the model checks in node and the rest in a headless browser, and installs
nothing either.

Data lives in a **separate private repo**, never in this one. The token is entered once in the
app, stored on the device, and scoped so it can only touch that data repo.

## Status

The main app, the sync layer and the on-device checks are done and verified end to end against a
real repo. The calendar is built — the five views, the kanban, the entry popup and its field
popups, the filter and the settings — and `test/run.sh` covers it.

Not built yet: the per-app summary above the tiles that [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md)
describes. The tile screen shows tiles only, so opening the calendar is currently the only way
to see what is on today.

    """`{+n}` is the row's own day plus n, as a date in the month being checked."""
    import re
    return re.sub(r"\{\+(\d+)\}",

  "2-linen|2. LINEN|Warm paper - Charter headings on off-white, terracotta accent, tinted event chips"

  "4-pebble|4. PEBBLE|Soft and rounded - rounded font, pill controls, big radii, indigo accent, roomier targets"

  "6-meridian|6. MERIDIAN|Quiet luxury - Palatino period label, forest and brass, small-caps labels, lots of air"
  "7-mono-ink|7. MONO-INK|Minimal product UI - black on white, 1px greys, layered shadows, 8% colour tints"

Eight directions, three shots each (month view, entry popup, kanban). Nothing in the repo was touched — no files changed, no tests run, no commits.

## The eight

| # | Name | The idea | Fonts | Entry chips | Icons |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Graphite** | Swiss neutral. Hairline rules, boxed outline nav buttons, near-monochrome chrome with one blue. | Helvetica Neue / Heros, tight tracking | Solid fill, desaturated slate / moss / plum | Outline, 1.4 |
| 2 | **Linen** | Warm paper. Off-white ground, Charter serif headings, terracotta accent. | Charter display + humanist sans body | Tinted + 2px colour rule | Outline, 1.2 |
| 3 | **Midnight** | Dark first. Navy page, lifted cells and cards, luminous tints, 15px radii. | System sans, −0.018em | Tinted on dark | Solid, 1.6 |
| 4 | **Pebble** | Soft and rounded. Rounded font, pill nav, 22px overlay radii, roomier targets. | SF Pro Rounded / Quicksand | Solid fill, friendly palette | Solid, 2.0, circular |
| 5 | **Blueprint** | Technical and dense. Real gridlines, mono figures, 2px corners, uppercase period. | Liberation Sans + mono numerals | Outlined, white, left bar | Outline, 1.3, square caps |
| 6 | **Meridian** | Quiet luxury. Palatino period label, forest + brass hairline, letterspaced caps, lots of air. | Pagella display + Cantarell | Tinted, earthy | Outline, 1.1, circular |
| 7 | **Mono-Ink** | Minimal product UI. Pure black on white, 1px greys, layered shadows, black today-pill. | Inter-class, −0.011em | 14% tint with colour as ink | Outline, 1.5 |
| 8 | **Aurora** | Modern and colourful. Violet primary, gradient topbar, colour-tinted kanban headers. | System sans, bold headings | Solid fill, saturated | Solid, 1.8, circular |

## What varies, and what I had to work around

- **Colours.** Each theme proposes its own *category* palette (work/home/health) and *stage* palette (todo/doing/done). The category colours live in your `groups.md` in the data repo, so adopting a theme means editing that file too — it is your data, not app code.
- **Fonts.** Your CSP is `default-src 'self'`, so no Google Fonts, no webfonts at all. Every stack is system fonts only. The shots render on this Linux box, so you are seeing the metric-compatible fallback (TeX Gyre Heros for Helvetica, Bitstream Charter for Charter, Pagella for Palatino, Quicksand for SF Pro Rounded); on your Mac/iPhone the first name in each stack wins and will look slightly better, not worse.
- **Icons.** Themes 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 swap the filled glyphs (trashcan, disk, house, ball, pin, person, bell, filter) for stroked outline versions — the single biggest change in how the icon row reads. The rest keep the current drawn set at a different weight and size. All of it stays inline SVG on the same 16×16 box.
- **Chip treatment** is the other big lever and is independent of the palette: solid fill (today's behaviour), tint-with-coloured-ink, or outlined-with-left-bar. Any theme can take any of the three.
- **Sizes** moved per theme: nav button size, period label 1.7–2.15rem, cell padding, entry line size, kanban card padding, overlay radii and shadows.

Two things I deliberately did **not** change, since they are behaviour rather than style: the period label format (`NOV/26`, and `2` for a sprint — spelling these out as "November 2026" and "Sprint 2" would help the professional read, say the word and I will), and the kanban's sprint-number-only header.

One caveat on the mocks: the fixture's token is intentionally invalid, so the live sync line says "token rejected". I overrode that text to a neutral in-sync line in the screenshots — the styling of that row is real, the message is not.

Unrelated: `.claude/settings.json` shows as modified in git. That is the `entire` CLI rewriting its own hook config at session start, not me; I left it alone.

Raw files: the 24 individual screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-max-ws-mine/249a9116-833b-48ce-a235-7c104668a764/scratchpad/skin/out/`, the theme definitions in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-max-ws-mine/249a9116-833b-48ce-a235-7c104668a764/scratchpad/skin/themes.mjs`. Tell me which direction to take — or which parts of which (e.g. "Mono-Ink's chrome with Graphite's palette and Blueprint's density") — and I will turn it into real CSS in `calendar/style.css` and `style.css`.

I like the 2) Linen. Implement it. Globally. But for task/event popup use a more intense background color for category/important/repeat/... icon when active. Also derive a nice color for the respective dark mode linen. Do run the excessive test. Once finished commit and push. I will review then on my phone/desktop.

**Entries** are now a tint of their category's colour with that colour as the ink and a full-strength rule down the left edge, instead of a solid block. `views.js` hands the colour to the stylesheet as `--c`; the two mixes are tokens, because a dark page needs more tint and a lighter ink.

**Active icons in the entry popup** light in their own field's colour, as you picked: the category in the colour it holds with the ball knocked out, `!` in the Linen red, everything else in the terracotta. The `24h`/`!` chips under the chevron carry the same two colours as tints.

**Dark Linen** is the same paper at night — warm near-black with brown in it (`#17130f`), paper ink, terracotta lifted to amber (`#e0a05c`). Two things couldn't follow the theme while they were hexes in JS, so both moved: the three stage colours are `var(--todo)`/`--doing`/`--done` with a value per theme, and the entry tint is a pair of `--chip-*` mixes applied to the one hex your data can carry.

## Things worth knowing

- **Your category colours live in your data repo, not here.** I set `calendar/sample/groups.md` to the Linen palette (brick `#8c3b2e`, moss `#5a6e3a`, teal `#2f5d6b`), but your real `groups.md` in `mine-data` still holds the old flat-UI colours. The tint treatment works with any hex, so nothing looks broken — but if you want the palette above, that file is a one-line-each edit on your side.
- **No web fonts.** Your CSP is `default-src 'self'`, so every stack is system fonts; Charter ships on macOS and iOS, and the fallback chain lands on Georgia elsewhere.
- **Two checks moved with the design.** A lit category icon is now verified for carrying the category's own colour rather than merely having a background, and the kanban stage colour is read off its property instead of the literal `#e0a500` — a hex is one theme's answer now. I updated `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md`, `TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md` and `calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md` to describe the new rules rather than the old ones.
- **One size I had to put back.** I'd grown the icon button to 2.2rem; that broke the invariant that an open field row is exactly as tall as a closed one (the row's fixed height is set by its trashcan). The glyph inside is larger, the box stayed 2.1rem.
- **`.claude/settings.json` is still uncommitted** — that is the `entire` CLI rewriting its own hook config, not part of this change, so I left it out of the commit.

One thing I deliberately left alone, since it is behaviour rather than style: the period label still reads `NOV/26`, and the kanban header still reads a bare `2` for the sprint. Spelling those out as "November 2026" and "Sprint 2" would help the professional read a lot — say the word and it is a small change.
